questions.q: What does named-patient supply actually mean?
questions.a: If a medicine is not registered or not available in your market, the named-patient pathway lets a treating physician request it for one identified patient. We source the product from a verified manufacturer and support the import permit and documentation the destination regulator requires.

questions.q: What documentation comes with a quote?
questions.a: Product specifications and the certification references that apply to each line — CE marking and CMDR approvals for devices, WHO-GMP credentials and Certificates of Analysis for pharmaceuticals, and ISO 9809-1 / DOT/TPED certification for gas cylinders. Documentation varies by product and destination market, so we state it line by line rather than as a blanket claim.

questions.q: Do we need an account or login to request a quote?
questions.a: No. Institutional requisitions and specialty-access requests are submitted directly through the contact workflow, and a case manager responds within 24 hours.

questions.q: How do you handle cold-chain products?
questions.a: Temperature-sensitive products ship in monitored packaging, with the temperature record and chain of custody documented from dispatch through to handover at the treating facility.

questions.q: Where do you source from, and where do you deliver?
questions.a: Sourcing runs through our India hub in New Delhi and logistics through our Philippines hub in Metro Manila, serving hospitals, clinics, and trade partners across more than 50 countries.

questions.q: What are your minimum order quantities and lead times?
questions.a: Both depend on the product category, volume, and destination market, so we confirm them on the quote rather than publishing a single figure. Send your line list and we will come back with quantities, lead times, and documentation together.

questions.q: Can you support tenders and framework agreements?
questions.a: Yes. Send the tender line list or framework schedule and we will quote against the stated specifications, flagging any line where an equivalent product or an alternative certification route is the better fit.
